submission.justification: Sensor-T3 has the best unirradiated resolution (6.0 um), but it fails the hard efficiency requirement. Its hit efficiency is 82.0% after 2e16 neq/cm^2 because of strong charge trapping and loss of full depletion, so it is ruled out. Of the two technologies that pass (T1 at 98.5%, T2 at 99.2%), the planar Sensor-T1 has clearly better resolution: 9.0 um versus 14.0 um in the 2025 simulation at 150 um. That makes T1 the best option that meets the constraints. I recommend 150 um because it is the only thickness with resolution data and it is inside the 50-300 um range. Caveats: (1) I had no simulation tool, so I did not run a thickness scan. (2) The test-beam document does not give the sensor thickness used for the efficiency measurements. (3) The resolution figures are for unirradiated sensors. Before final sign-off, efficiency at 2e16 should be confirmed for T1 at exactly 150 um.

requirements.requirement: Goal: best possible single-hit spatial resolution
requirements.evidence: T1 has the best resolution of the technologies that pass the efficiency requirement: 9.0 um vs 14.0 um for T2 (2025 simulation, 150 um, unirradiated). T3 (6.0 um) is excluded by the efficiency requirement. Resolution after irradiation has not been checked.
